title: Tartu founded as Yuryev
description: Yaroslav the Wise of Kiev builds a fort named Yuryev, the first record of Tartu.

title: Battle of St. Matthew's Day
description: German crusaders and their allies defeat the Estonians and kill their leader Lembitu.

title: Tallinn receives Lübeck law
description: King Eric IV of Denmark grants Tallinn the town law of Lübeck, tying it to the Hanseatic trading world.

title: St. George's Night Uprising
description: Estonians rise against their Danish and German lords and are crushed over the next two years by the Teutonic Order.

title: Denmark sells northern Estonia
description: King Valdemar IV sells the Duchy of Estonia to the Teutonic Order, ending over a century of Danish rule.

title: First surviving printed book in Estonian
description: A Lutheran catechism by Simon Wanradt and Johann Koell is printed, the oldest book in Estonian of which pages survive.

title: Livonian War begins
description: Ivan IV of Russia invades Livonia and takes Narva and Tartu, starting a war that ends the medieval order in Estonia and Latvia.

title: University of Tartu founded
description: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden founds a university at Tartu, the oldest in Estonia.

title: Great Famine
description: Cold, wet summers ruin the harvests and about a fifth of the population dies.

title: Estonia surrenders to Russia
description: Tallinn and the Estonian nobility capitulate to Peter the Great, beginning two centuries of Russian rule.

title: Serfdom abolished
description: Peasants in the Governorate of Estonia are freed from serfdom, though without land.

title: Kalevipoeg published
description: Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald's verse epic appears in instalments and becomes the Estonian national epic.

title: First Estonian Song Festival
description: Choirs from across the country gather for the first national song festival, a founding event of the national awakening.

title: Declaration of independence
description: The Salvation Committee proclaims the Republic of Estonia between the Russian retreat and the arrival of German troops.

title: War of Independence begins
description: The Red Army attacks Narva, opening a war in which Estonia holds its independence against Soviet Russia and the Baltic German forces.

title: Treaty of Tartu with Soviet Russia
description: Soviet Russia recognises Estonian independence and gives up all claims to its territory.

title: Communist coup attempt
description: An armed rising organised from the Soviet Union is put down within hours.

title: Päts takes emergency powers
description: Konstantin Päts declares a state of emergency to block the Vaps movement, beginning six years of authoritarian rule.

title: Soviet occupation
description: The Red Army occupies Estonia after an ultimatum, and the country is annexed to the Soviet Union in August.

title: Soviet forces retake Tallinn
description: The Red Army enters Tallinn days after an Estonian government had tried to restore independence, and Soviet rule returns.

title: March deportation
description: Soviet security forces begin deporting about 90,000 people from Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania to Siberia to break resistance to collective farming.

title: Song of Estonia
description: About 300,000 people gather to sing national songs and hear open calls for independence, the height of the Singing Revolution.

title: Declaration of sovereignty
description: The Supreme Soviet of Estonia declares its laws supreme over those of the Soviet Union, the first Soviet republic to do so.

title: Independence restored
description: During the coup attempt in Moscow the Supreme Council declares Estonian independence restored.

title: Sinking of the MS Estonia
place: Baltic Sea, south of Utö, Finland
description: The ferry Estonia sinks in a storm on the way from Tallinn to Stockholm and 852 people die.

title: Estonia joins the European Union
description: Estonia enters the European Union, a month after joining NATO.

title: Bronze Night
description: The removal of a Soviet war memorial sets off two nights of rioting and a wave of cyberattacks on Estonian institutions.

title: Estonia adopts the euro
description: The euro replaces the kroon, making Estonia the first former Soviet republic in the eurozone.
